title: 10 Most Popular Restaurants in Nong Khai 2026 — Mekong Riverfront, Authentic Vietnamese, Mekong Fish | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: The 10 most popular restaurants in Nong Khai 2026 — from the legendary Daeng Nam Nueng to Krua Mae Paed's giant fried river shrimp, Chaiyakhong local food, Mae Ut Vietnamese, all the way to Macky's Riverside Kitchen. Signature dishes, prices, and location for each spot.

ogTitle: 10 Most Popular Restaurants in Nong Khai 2026 — Eat Like a Local
ogDesc: Legendary nam nueng, fresh Mekong fish, and sunset riverside restaurants — the 10 most talked-about spots in Nong Khai, with signature dishes and prices for every one.
intro: Nong Khai is a Mekong riverfront city that eats far better than its size lets on — authentic Vietnamese nam nueng, freshly caught Mekong fish, and riverside restaurants where you can sit and watch the sun go down for as long as you like. We've gathered the 10 spots that locals and travelers mention most, from legendary old-timers to newly opened Mekong-view cafés. Pick your meal and budget, and go.
chips: 🍤 Authentic nam nueng — the original recipe

blocks.html:
When people think of eating in Nong Khai, two things come up first: "Vietnamese food" and "Mekong fish." The city sits on the river directly across from Vientiane, so it's absorbed Vietnamese food culture completely — nam nueng, kuay jap yuan, fried spring rolls, pak mo, all the way to rich Saigon-style coffee. Stroll along Tha Sadet market on the riverfront in the evening and you'll find restaurants lined up catching the river breeze, some with live music, some in creaky old wooden houses that have been selling the same dishes for decades. For a more relaxed vibe, the Hat Kham and Wiangkhuk zones have Mekong-view cafés where you can sit all day.

This list includes genuine legends — Daeng Nam Nueng, the original riverside branch that's been making nam nueng for over 40 years and holds a 5-star OTOP food award many years running. Krua Mae Paed on the Mueang Mi riverside stretch, famous for giant fried river shrimp. Chaiyakhong restaurant, open over 30 years, with bold local dishes like laab pla khaeng and tom som pla khang. Mae Ut Vietnamese, the longtime original on Soi Michai still using an antique brass pan to make Vietnamese-egg pizza. And Macky's Riverside Kitchen, the Thai-Western Mekong spot where backpackers return for the fish and chips. Pick a restaurant and go taste it yourself.

blocks.name: Daeng Nam Nueng (Original Branch, Riverside)
blocks.area: Mueang Nong Khai District, Nong Khai
blocks.signature: Nam nueng set, shrimp wrapped in sugar cane, krayaw fritters, stuffed pork leg
blocks.descHtml:
If you visit Nong Khai and haven't stopped at "Daeng Nam Nueng" — the original riverside branch near Tha Sadet market — you haven't really arrived. The restaurant has been open since 1968, founded by a Vietnamese immigrant family who settled here, and has become the city's de facto welcome table. Great for families, groups of friends, or anyone wanting to try authentic nam nueng from the original source. The building is a large open hall with a seating zone overlooking the Mekong with views across to Laos. Wide parking at several spots. It gets busy on most days but there's plenty of seating so the wait is rarely long.

The dish to order is the nam nueng set — it comes with fragrant grilled minced pork patties, soft rice paper sheets, a mountain of fresh vegetables, and the house dipping sauce that many people consider the real star. You wrap it yourself bite by bite, which is half the fun. There's also shrimp wrapped in sugar cane (the shrimp is springy and sweet with a subtle cane fragrance), crispy-outside soft-inside krayaw fritters, and stuffed pork leg that nearly every table orders. Fried spring rolls and pork ribs round it out if you want more.

Reviews consistently praise the freshness of the vegetables (partly home-grown), the well-rounded dipping sauce, and the generous portions for the price. The nam nueng set starts around 220 THB for a small portion, 320 THB for a large, averaging roughly 100–250 THB per person. One common note: it gets extremely packed during peak hours and the car park fills up fast — if you're coming on a weekend, arriving earlier in the day is wise.

Open daily around 06:00–20:30. Takeaway is available from early morning; dine-in starts around 08:00. Located on the riverside road near the entrance to Tha Sadet market — easy to continue the day with a market stroll afterward. The reason this place never loses its popularity: over 50 years of being the original, consistent cooking, and a souvenir people buy to take home all year round.
blocks.bestFor: First meal in the province, family and group visits

blocks.name: Ca Phe Viet
blocks.area: Tha Sadet market, riverside road, Mueang Nong Khai District, Nong Khai
blocks.signature: Kuay jap yuan (Vietnamese noodle soup), tam kuay jap, crispy pork miang, Saigon coffee, bingsu
blocks.descHtml:
If you're in Nong Khai and want authentic Vietnamese food on the river in an old-town setting, Ca Phe Viet inside Tha Sadet market is the name locals and visitors mention most. The restaurant occupies a riverside building with two floors — the upper floor looks out over the Mekong and across to Laos, making it ideal for anyone who wants both good food and a view in the same meal. Finish shopping for souvenirs at the Tha Sadet market downstairs and head upstairs to rest.

The dish almost every table orders is kuay jap yuan (Vietnamese rice noodle soup) — soft noodles in a rounded, savory broth. Tam kuay jap (spiced noodle salad) gets unanimous praise in reviews as something you'll order again. Then crispy pork miang, Vietnamese sausage, and pak mo yuan, which many people describe as perfectly soft and crisp. For som tam fans, try the Luang Prabang-style version here. Finish with strong, fragrant Saigon coffee or cool bingsu — reviews love it as a sweet cool-down after a heavy meal.

Reviews mostly run positive — bold Vietnamese-Isan fusion flavors, polite service, and large generous portions. At 101–250 THB per person it sits in the mid-range; some note the prices have crept up a little but the Mekong view and atmosphere make it worthwhile.

Worth knowing: the restaurant opens midday through evening (roughly 08:00–18:00 daily — check the Facebook page before long holidays). Many reviewers suggest late afternoon to evening for the best riverside atmosphere. On holidays it fills up fast, so arrive early if you want an upstairs window table. The restaurant sells Vietnamese souvenirs on the ground floor too.
blocks.bestFor: Riverside lunch or dinner, Vietnamese food lovers

blocks.name: Chaiyakhong Restaurant
blocks.area: Mueang Nong Khai District, Nong Khai
blocks.signature: Laab pla khaeng, tom som pla khang, gaeng khua hoy khom, yam yot maphrao, pla buek phat cha
blocks.descHtml:
Chaiyakhong is one of Nong Khai's oldest riverside restaurants, open for several decades and long considered one of the first names locals think of when they want serious local food. The building is a large old wooden house on the riverside irrigation bank, looking out over the wide river toward distant Laos. Ideal for anyone wanting relaxed open-air dining with a river breeze and Mekong fish dishes that are hard to find in larger cities. A great first stop for anyone new to Nong Khai who wants genuinely local flavors.

The signature dishes people order most are laab pla khaeng — fish minced with roasted chili powder and toasted rice in a home-style preparation, with a pronounced toasted-rice fragrance — and tom som pla khang, a pure Isan sour broth packed with galangal and lemongrass. There's also gaeng khua hoy khom (fresh snail curry), yam yot maphrao (fresh coconut shoot salad, bold and tangy), and pla buek phat cha (giant catfish stir-fry, spicy and hot). Reviews consistently praise the bold, authentic Isan-local seasoning, adjustable spice levels, and the freshness of the river fish as the reason people return.

Prices are mid-range — roughly 250–500 THB per person when ordering several dishes to share. Standout dishes like the snail curry or coconut shoot salad run around 190–220 THB. Great for families or groups sharing dishes at the table. Located on Kaew Worawut Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Nong Khai — not far from the town center. Open daily mid-morning through evening. A riverside evening meal with the breeze running through is when the restaurant is at its best.

The restaurant earns its popularity by combining three things: Mekong river views, hard-to-find local fish dishes, and the trust of longtime local customers. Worth knowing: some reviews mention that on very busy days food can come out slower and ingredient freshness can vary — a weekday evening is recommended for the most comfortable experience. Arrive before sunset if you want a good water-view table.
blocks.bestFor: Evening riverside dinner with family or a group of friends

blocks.name: Jin San Pan Egg
blocks.area: Mueang Nong Khai District, Nong Khai
blocks.signature: Pan egg, stuffed bread, kuay jap yuan, fresh coffee
blocks.descHtml:
If you wake up early in Nong Khai and aren't sure where to eat, "Jin San Pan Egg" is the long-running local favorite. The shop sits on the riverside road, just past Nong Khai Hospital, near the Red Cross and the Governor's Residence, directly across from Cake at Teoy café — a Vietnamese-meets-café breakfast spot that's been open for years. Perfect for anyone wanting to start the day with a warm, wallet-friendly meal, whether you're a local or a traveler exploring the riverside.

The dish to order is the "pan egg" — served in a hot pan, yolk perfectly runny, topped with minced pork, Chinese sausage, and pork floss. Dip the warm French bread into the yolk for a great combination. Reviews consistently praise the egg for not being dry or burnt, with a gentle buttery aroma. The "stuffed bread" is crisp outside and soft inside. Another frequently ordered item is "kuay jap yuan" — rounded broth fragrant with pepper, with melt-tender pork bones. Finish with "fresh coffee," which many say pairs perfectly with the morning. On some Saturday–Sunday mornings there's also a pork stew with a rich broth added to the menu.

Prices are very reasonable — under 100 THB per person. The pan egg starts at around 30 THB, bread from 10 THB a piece, coffee 30–40 THB. The interior is a clean, bright white space, open and comfortable with only a few tables, giving the feeling of eating at a friend's home. The owner is welcoming and easy-going — that warmth is part of why people keep coming back.

Open daily from about 07:00 to 16:00 (some days a little earlier). Worth knowing: on holiday mornings it gets busy and food can come out a bit slower since everything is cooked fresh to order, one pan at a time. Allow time to sit back, then walk along the riverside afterward. If you want a simple, affordable, and satisfying breakfast in Nong Khai, this is the place to mark on your map.

blocks.name: Mae Ut Vietnamese and Bakery
blocks.area: Mueang Nong Khai District, Nong Khai
blocks.signature: Vietnamese pizza with egg, banh bao, khao kriap pak mo, fried spring rolls
blocks.descHtml:
When it comes to old-school Vietnamese food in Nong Khai, many people think of "Mae Ut Vietnamese and Bakery" — a long-running shop on Soi Michai, across from Wat Si Samang, that has been making food this way for decades and is well-known to the people of Nong Khai. The standout is that everything is made fresh in front of you — the grandmother and her son sit out making pak mo and toasting sesame rice crackers in plain view. If you like Vietnamese food that's homemade and lightly seasoned, this is the right place.

The dish almost every table orders is Vietnamese pizza with egg — a thin fragrant crust with a generous topping. Next is khao kriap pak mo, which reviews praise for being homemade, thin and soft, with a generous filling. Then banh bao (Vietnamese steamed rice cups) topped with crispy garlic and pork crackling, and fried spring rolls that come out hot and non-greasy. The dominant consensus in reviews: "looks homey but tastes extraordinary" — the dipping sauce is a standout that makes the whole meal work.

Prices are very friendly — many people order three dishes for around 150 THB and leave full. Popular items start in the low tens of baht through the low hundreds per dish. The setting is a comfortable open-air shop, with take-home items on display too. One note from reviews: the midday period can feel hot, and on busy days there can be a short wait.

Open approximately 10:00–18:00 nearly every day. Located on Soi Michai, about one kilometer past Tha Sadet market. Parking at the temple lot across the road. For anyone in Nong Khai who wants Vietnamese food the way locals actually eat it, this is the place. Mid-morning through early afternoon is the sweet spot — the menu is fully stocked and you won't risk anything selling out.
blocks.bestFor: Mid-morning to afternoon, original Vietnamese food

blocks.name: Krua Mae Paed
blocks.area: Mueang Nong Khai District, Nong Khai
blocks.signature: Giant fried river shrimp, mok phung pla Mekong, tom yam pla khang, laab pla khang, nam phrik sam sa-hai
blocks.descHtml:
If you're in Nong Khai and want fresh Mekong fish right on the river, Krua Mae Paed is one of the most frequently mentioned names among both locals and travelers. The restaurant sits on Route 244, the Nong Khai–Tha Bo riverside road, around kilometer marker 9 before Wat Si Chomchuen. Tables are right at the water's edge with views across to Laos. Perfect for families, groups of friends, or anyone who wants to sit with older relatives for a long relaxed meal watching the sunset over the river.

Almost every table orders the "giant fried river shrimp" — fresh shrimp fried crisp in a bundle, cooked in fresh oil until dry and non-greasy, starting around 150 THB. Another signature is "mok phung pla Mekong" (around 150–200 THB), fragrant with herbs and rich from the fish belly, and the "nam phrik sam sa-hai set" (around 120 THB) that comes with a mound of fresh vegetables. For bold Isan flavors, try the tom yam pla khang clear broth and laab pla khang, plus soft-fleshed fish fried with garlic and dancing shrimp. Reviews consistently praise the freshness, the firm fish flesh, and the full-strength authentic Isan seasoning.

The atmosphere is a real selling point — a wide restaurant with plenty of seating and a riverside terrace to catch the cool breeze in the shade, with Mekong sunset views beautiful enough that people come specifically for photos. Prices are mid-range, around 251–500 THB per person for large fish dishes or shared orders. Parking available, credit cards accepted. The review score on food sites runs around 3.8 stars, with most praise going to the views and the fish freshness.

Worth knowing: open daily approximately 09:00–21:00. Weekend evenings are busy with the best views — for large groups or a riverside table, calling ahead to book is recommended. Some fish are priced by weight — ask before ordering to keep track of the bill.
blocks.bestFor: Evening riverside dinner with family or friends
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: larb · Takeaway / Wikimedia (CC BY-SA 3.0)

blocks.name: Wiangchan Restaurant
blocks.area: Wiangkhuk, Mueang Nong Khai District (toward Tha Bo), Nong Khai
blocks.signature: Pla nuea on fried with garlic, tom yam pla khang, pla khang blanched with jaew, steamed fish
blocks.descHtml:
If you're in Nong Khai and want fresh Mekong river fish in a way you won't find in the city, Wiangchan Restaurant is where people in this area bring each other regularly. The restaurant is on the Mekong riverside in Wiangkhuk, about 10 km from Nong Khai town toward Tha Bo. Tables face the river with a clear view across to Laos. A true river-fish restaurant suited to large family groups, friend groups, or anyone who wants to sit and relax by the water.

Almost every table orders pla nuea on fried with garlic — crisp outside, tender inside, fragrant with fried garlic. And pla khang blanched with jaew — firm, springy flesh dipped in a bold jaew sauce. For those who want a hot broth, the tom yam pla khang is bold and savory. Steamed fish is another regular order — fresh fish with fragrant herbs, sweet flesh. Round it out with nam nueng and Luang Prabang-style som tam. Reviews consistently say the fish is genuinely fresh, the cooking is on point, and it suits guest-hosting occasions well.

Prices run roughly 251–500 THB per person — fair for fresh river fish. The standout pla nuea on fried with garlic starts around 200 THB per dish, better value shared across a group. Open daily from mid-morning through evening. Parking available, indoor and riverside sala seating. The Wongnai score runs around 4.3 stars, reflecting a loyal base of repeat customers.

Worth knowing: the restaurant is outside town — driving is the most practical way to get there. Weekend evenings fill up — for large groups a call ahead to book a river-view table is the right call. For anyone who likes easy river-fish dining without a rush, this place delivers.
mustOrder: Pla nuea on fried with garlic
blocks.bestFor: River fish meal with family or friends, guest hosting

blocks.name: Macky's Riverside Kitchen
blocks.area: Riverside promenade, near the west entrance to Tha Sadet market, Mueang Nong Khai District, Nong Khai
blocks.signature: Fish and chips, burgers, pies, Thai and European dishes
blocks.descHtml:
If you're walking the Mekong promenade near Tha Sadet market and fancy fish and chips or a burger, Macky's Riverside Kitchen is the first name that comes to mind for Nong Khai locals and visiting foreigners alike. The restaurant has been open since 2015, run by Macky and family, serving both serious Western food and Thai-Isan dishes — which makes it work for travelers missing a taste of home and Thais curious about something different on the river.

The most frequently reordered dish is fish and chips — moist, flaky fish inside, thin crisp batter, with many reviews calling it "nearly perfect." The meat and mushroom pie gets praise for a full, rich filling. The beef burger comes generously loaded. For morning visitors there's granola yogurt with fruit. The coffee here earns good mentions too. The Thai side of the menu covers a range of options, including vegetarian dishes.

The real draw is the location and atmosphere. The restaurant sits on the Mekong promenade near the west entrance to Tha Sadet market, with outdoor tables looking over the river and across to Laos. Cool breezes in the evening, beautiful sunset views. Live music plays Sunday through Friday evenings from around 7pm to 9:30pm. Free Wi-Fi. Reviewers consistently note it's clean, quiet, and the staff are friendly and easy to talk to. Prices run about 70–300 THB per person — fair for freshly cooked Western food in a small city.

Google rating runs around 4.4 from several hundred reviews, and it consistently ranks at the top of Nong Khai restaurant lists. Open daily approximately 07:00–21:00. Weekend evenings fill up fast — for groups or if you want a riverside sunset table, allowing extra time or calling ahead is a good move.
blocks.bestFor: Evening riverside sunset dining / Western food lovers

blocks.name: Yam Yen Nong Khai
blocks.area: Hat Kham Subdistrict, Mueang Nong Khai District, Nong Khai
blocks.signature: Thai–Isan snacks and sides, drinks and café, sunset viewing spot
blocks.descHtml:
Yam Yen Nong Khai is a restaurant-café hybrid on the Mekong riverside in Hat Kham, Mueang Nong Khai — its name translates roughly as "evening time," and it does exactly what that name promises: an atmosphere that shines when the sun softens and casts orange light across the Mekong, with a clear view across to Laos. This is the spot for anyone wanting a long, unhurried evening after work, couples looking for a scenic backdrop, or a group of friends who want to share Isan snacks over drinks. The restaurant has multiple seating zones — air-conditioned inside and an open-air riverside terrace catching the cool breeze. The wooden sign out front has a warm, welcoming feel.

The menu spans Isan snacks and sides through café drinks. Popular food items lean Isan: laab, fishballs, sausage, stir-fries, and soups — easy-ordering, easy-eating dishes that go well with drinks. For those who want Mekong river dishes, there are fish options too. On the café side there's coffee, fresh milk, and desserts like bread with ice cream and green tea latte. After dark there are also alcoholic beverages. Reviews consistently describe the food as solid, the staff as warm and relaxed, and the prices as fair compared to the view you're getting.

Located on the Mekong riverside in Hat Kham, just a short drive from the town center. Open daily 11:00–24:00. Bookings: 065-449-5547 — weekend evenings fill up, so calling ahead to reserve a riverside spot is worthwhile. The restaurant has soft background music that adds a romantic touch for those who want to sit late into the night.

The real selling point of Yam Yen is timing — if you want a beautiful sunset shot, arrive before the sun drops to claim your spot and order before it gets busy, as riverside seats go fast. Those who don't enjoy the open heat can sit in the air-conditioned section and step outside for photos when the light turns golden. Easy to get to, gentle on the wallet, and you get the full Mekong view in one place.

blocks.name: Thai Baan Rimkhong
blocks.area: Hat Kham Subdistrict, Mueang Nong Khai District, Nong Khai
blocks.signature: Grilled sai yang, Thai–Isan sides at budget prices (~79 THB/dish)
blocks.descHtml:
Thai Baan Rimkhong is a newer Thai–Isan restaurant in Hat Kham subdistrict, just a short drive from Nong Khai town, with full Mekong river views. It's been talked about among locals and travelers since it opened, because it pulls off something rare — a genuinely beautiful riverside setting with prices that are actually easy on the wallet. Perfect for anyone who wants to sit and eat a relaxed evening meal with music playing softly in the background and the Mekong in front of them. Works for two, for families, or for a full group.

What keeps people coming back is the single fixed price of 79 THB per dish across nearly every item on the menu — order multiple things to share without any bill anxiety. The dish everyone points to as a must-try is grilled sai yang — aromatic off the grill, skin crisp, meat inside soft and tender, excellent with jaew dipping sauce. A lot of people reorder it. The rest of the menu covers Isan sides and à la carte Thai food. Eat with hot sticky rice and the whole thing is straightforward, honest, and true to the restaurant's name.

The setting is the other strong point — tables face the river, evening light is beautiful for photos, and the breezes are cool. Open daily from 10:00 to midnight, covering late lunch, dinner, and a late-night option. If you want a riverside table at sunset, arriving early or calling ahead is wise as it fills up on holiday evenings.

The short version: if you're in Nong Khai and want a satisfying, affordable meal with a Mekong view, Thai Baan Rimkhong delivers. A newcomer that's earned its following fast and is worth the stop.
blocks.bestFor: Relaxed riverside evening on a budget, with a group

blocks.title: What to know before you eat in Nong Khai

items.title: Walk the Tha Sadet zone
items.text: Many of the top restaurants are along the riverside road and near Tha Sadet market — easy walking distance from each other. Mekong fish restaurants in the Mueang Mi or Wiangkhuk zones are outside town — Grab or a rented motorbike or car is more convenient for those.

items.title: Carry cash
items.text: Street food stalls, breakfast spots, and small riverside shacks mostly accept cash only. Some larger restaurants offer PromptPay, but carrying small-denomination Thai baht is the safest approach.

items.title: Arrive before sunset for a good view
items.text: Riverside tables at popular restaurants fill up from 5–6pm, especially on holidays. If you want a sunset seat, arrive early or call ahead to book.

items.title: Ask the size before ordering fish
items.text: Mekong fish restaurants price whole fish by size and weight. Ask for the approximate weight and price before ordering — especially for pla khang and large pla nuea on.

items.title: English menus available at some spots
items.text: Western spots like Macky's have English menus and English-speaking staff. Local restaurants may only have Thai menus — pointing at food photos or using a translation app works well. Nong Khai people are friendly and always happy to help.

items.title: Tipping
items.text: Tipping is not expected at local restaurants. Leaving small change or 20–50 THB at a place that gave you good service is a nice gesture. Some larger restaurants may already include a service charge — check the bill.

blocks.title: Planning your eating in Nong Khai in one day
blocks.html:
Start breakfast at Jin San Pan Egg — order the pan egg, stuffed bread, and fresh coffee for under 100 THB per person. A good start before heading out. Mid-morning, swing by Daeng Nam Nueng's original riverside branch to eat nam nueng and shrimp wrapped in sugar cane on-site or buy it as a take-home gift. For lunch, try the bold local flavors at Chaiyakhong Restaurant — laab pla khaeng and tom som pla khang.

In the afternoon, if you want serious Mekong fish, drive out to Krua Mae Paed on the Mueang Mi riverside for giant fried river shrimp and tom yam pla khang, or head to Wiangchan Restaurant in Wiangkhuk for pla nuea on fried with garlic. Wrap up the evening in the Hat Kham zone at Yam Yen Nong Khai or Thai Baan Rimkhong — sit with a drink and watch the sun go down over the river. For a more Western vibe, Macky's Riverside Kitchen near Tha Sadet has live music most evenings.

blocks.text: Making a full day of eating in Nong Khai? Staying a night by the river is far more relaxing than driving back — you can wander Tha Sadet market in the evening and watch the sunset without rushing.

faq.q: Which restaurant is most famous in Nong Khai?
faq.a: By reputation, Daeng Nam Nueng — the original riverside branch — is the first name most people say. It's been making nam nueng for over 40 years and holds a 5-star OTOP food award for multiple consecutive years. For Mekong fish on the riverside, Krua Mae Paed and Chaiyakhong Restaurant are the names locals mention equally often.

faq.q: What are the signature foods of Nong Khai?
faq.a: The standouts are Vietnamese food — especially nam nueng, shrimp wrapped in sugar cane, krayaw fritters, fried spring rolls, and kuay jap yuan. The second strong suit is fresh Mekong fish: pla khang, pla nuea on, and river shrimp prepared as tom yam, garlic-fried, steamed, or laab. For breakfast, pan egg with stuffed bread is the local favorite.

faq.q: How much does food cost in Nong Khai?
faq.a: Breakfast at Jin San Pan Egg runs around 30–100 THB per person. General à la carte and Vietnamese restaurants like Daeng Nam Nueng or Mae Ut run about 50–250 THB per person. For Mekong fish restaurants like Krua Mae Paed, Chaiyakhong, or Wiangchan, ordering whole large fish puts the bill at around 250–500 THB per person, depending on fish size.

faq.q: Do I need to book a table ahead?
faq.a: On weekdays most restaurants are walk-in. But popular riverside spots like Krua Mae Paed, Yam Yen, or Macky's on holiday evenings and during festivals get packed. If you want a riverside sunset table, calling ahead or arriving before 6pm is the safest approach.

faq.q: Which places are open in the evening or late at night?
faq.a: The Hat Kham zone stays open late — Yam Yen opens from the afternoon through midnight, great for a long evening. Chaiyakhong is open until 10pm. Macky's has live music most evenings. Mekong fish restaurants like Krua Mae Paed close around 9pm. Breakfast spots like Jin San and Daeng Nam Nueng close early in the evening.
